In S_SS the overcurrent window trip is tested before the hard faults, so a shutdown is outranked by a hiccup
In S_RUN the overcurrent window trip is tested before the hard faults
In S_HICCUP the end of the cool-down is tested before the hard faults, so a retry outranks a shutdown
S_HICCUP exits on the soft-start handshake SS_done (copied from the S_SS block) instead of on hiccup_done
An overcurrent window trip during soft start is treated as a hard fault and sends the FSM to S_OFF instead of into the S_HICCUP cool-down
Reset puts the FSM in the S_HICCUP cool-down rather than S_OFF, as if power-up should wait a cool-down before the first start

runs.reason: the per-state enable mutants combined: a host (AIM.41) or switch (AIM.76) disable ignored in S_SS, S_RUN and S_HICCUP gives the same wrong state as AIM.46/15/47 or AIM.55/50/56, so any test that kills one of those kills it
descriptions: The host enable over SPI is treated as a start request checked only in S_OFF, so a host disable while ramping, running or in hiccup is ignored
The physical switch en_SW is treated as a start request checked only in S_OFF, so turning it off while ramping, running or in hiccup is ignored

runs.reason: the per-fault S_HICCUP mutants combined: a hard fault or disable that leaves the FSM in S_HICCUP, as AIM.39, AIM.40, AIM.57, AIM.58 and AIM.67 each do for one input, so any test that kills one of those kills it
descriptions: S_HICCUP has no hard-fault exit: the designer relied on the gate drive already being off and only waits for hiccup_done

runs.reason: line 135 sets next_state = state and every case branch assigns next_state (the default too), so the opening default and the per-state 'stay here' assignments are redundant
the deleted S_OFF or S_HICCUP item falls to the default, which also assigns en_from_state = 0
state_t is 2 bits and S_OFF/S_SS/S_RUN/S_HICCUP use all four codes (00, 01, 10, 11), and state is only ever loaded from reset or next_state, so the default arms never run
CIS swaps both labels, S_SS and S_RUN, and both items assign en_from_state = 1, so every state decodes as before; the AI judgement read it as relabelling one line only

AIM.1.description: S_HICCUP has no hard-fault exit: the designer relied on the gate drive already being off and only waits for hiccup_done
AIM.1.before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (hiccup_done) begin
AIM.1.reason: A hard fault or loss of g_en during the cool-down leaves the FSM in S_HICCUP (hiccup_active high, state_out = S_HICCUP) until hiccup_done, then it goes to S_SS, instead of going to S_OFF at once.
AIM.1.withdrawn: the per-fault S_HICCUP mutants combined: a hard fault or disable that leaves the FSM in S_HICCUP, as AIM.39, AIM.40, AIM.57, AIM.58 and AIM.67 each do for one input, so any test that kills one of those kills it

AIM.2.description: Start-up from S_OFF checks only the enable and none of the hard faults, relying on en being fault-gated
AIM.2.reason: With g_en high and OTP, UVLO, latch_state or latch_assert present, the FSM leaves S_OFF for S_SS, then is forced back, so state_out and ss_active toggle OFF/SS every other clock instead of staying in S_OFF.

AIM.3.description: S_OFF starts straight into S_RUN when SS_done is still high, skipping the re-ramp
AIM.3.reason: If SS_done is high when the converter is enabled from S_OFF, run_active rises and ss_active never does, so the soft-start ramp is skipped, violating the rule that every start re-ramps.

AIM.4.description: The power-stage enable is decoded from next_state instead of the registered state
AIM.4.reason: en rises one clock early on start from S_OFF (while state_out is still S_OFF) and drops one clock early on a window trip, so en no longer matches the registered state.

AIM.5.description: Telemetry state_out shows the next state instead of the present registered state
AIM.5.reason: On any transition state_out changes one clock before ss_active/run_active/hiccup_active, e.g. it reads S_SS while still in S_OFF when enable is applied.

AIM.6.description: run_active is decoded as 'power stage switching' and so is also high in S_SS
AIM.6.reason: During soft start run_active and ss_active are both high, instead of run_active being high only in S_RUN.

AIM.7.description: The gate-drive enable relies on the state alone for the hard faults, dropping the combinational fault gating
AIM.7.reason: When OTP, UVLO, latch_state or latch_assert asserts in S_SS or S_RUN, en stays high for one more clock until the FSM registers S_OFF, instead of dropping on the same clock.

AIM.8.description: ss_active is dropped as soon as the ramp reports done, a clock before the FSM leaves S_SS
AIM.8.reason: On the clock in S_SS where SS_done is high, ss_active is low while state_out is still S_SS; with SS_done held and window_trip_SS asserted, ss_active is low throughout S_SS.

AIM.9.description: An overcurrent window trip in S_RUN re-ramps straight into S_SS instead of first serving the S_HICCUP cool-down
AIM.9.reason: When window_trip asserts in S_RUN, the next state is S_SS. ss_active rises instead of hiccup_active, and en stays high, so the converter keeps switching with no cool-down.

AIM.10.description: At the end of the cool-down S_HICCUP returns to S_OFF and relies on S_OFF to restart, instead of retrying directly into S_SS
AIM.10.reason: After hiccup_done, state_out shows S_OFF for one clock and ss_active/en rise a clock late. hiccup_active falls without ss_active rising on the same edge.

AIM.11.description: hiccup_active is decoded from next_state, so it leads the registered S_HICCUP state by one clock
AIM.11.reason: hiccup_active rises on the same clock that window_trip or window_trip_SS asserts, while state_out still shows S_RUN or S_SS. It falls on the hiccup_done clock, a clock before the state leaves S_HICCUP.

AIM.12.description: run_active is taken as 'regulating and gate drive on', so the combinational fault gating of en also drops it
AIM.12.reason: In S_RUN, when OTP, UVLO, latch_state, latch_assert or loss of g_en asserts, run_active falls on the same clock. In the original it falls on the next clock, with state_out still showing S_RUN in between.

AIM.13.description: hiccup_active is decoded as 'power stage held off by the state', so it is also high in S_OFF
AIM.13.reason: Out of reset and whenever the FSM sits in S_OFF, hiccup_active is high although the state is not S_HICCUP. This starts the hiccup timer and strike counter while the converter is off.

AIM.14.description: The overcurrent window trips are treated as hard fault inputs in the combinational gating of en
AIM.14.reason: On the clock where window_trip (in S_RUN) or window_trip_SS (in S_SS) asserts, en goes low while the state is still S_RUN or S_SS. In the original, en stays high until S_HICCUP registers.

AIM.15.description: In S_RUN only the physical switch is checked for disable: a host disable over SPI gates en but does not send the FSM to S_OFF
AIM.15.before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | UVLO | latch_assert) begin
AIM.15.after: if (~en_SW | latch_state | OTP | UVLO | latch_assert) begin
AIM.15.reason: If spi_enable drops in S_RUN with en_SW high, en goes low but state stays S_RUN and run_active stays high. When spi_enable returns, en comes straight back at full duty without the S_SS re-ramp.

AIM.16.description: In S_SS ramp completion outranks the overcurrent window trip: window_trip_SS is only honoured while SS_done is low
AIM.16.reason: When fault_arbiter raises window_trip_SS on the same clock that soft_start raises SS_done, the FSM goes to S_RUN instead of S_HICCUP, so run_active rises and hiccup_active stays low, en stays high, and the cool-down is skipped.

AIM.17.description: In S_SS an overcurrent window trip outranks a hard fault, so a coincident shutdown is first sent through S_HICCUP
AIM.17.before: if (~g_en | OTP | latch_state | UVLO | latch_assert) begin
AIM.17.after: if ((~g_en | OTP | latch_state | UVLO | latch_assert) & ~window_trip_SS) begin
AIM.17.reason: If a hard fault (OTP, UVLO, latch, latch_assert or loss of enable) arrives on the same clock as window_trip_SS in S_SS, the FSM enters S_HICCUP instead of S_OFF. hiccup_active and state_out show S_HICCUP for a clock, and strike_counter counts a strike.

AIM.18.description: In S_RUN the overcurrent window trip outranks a hard fault, so a coincident shutdown goes to S_HICCUP first
AIM.18.before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | UVLO | latch_assert) begin
AIM.18.after: if ((~g_en | latch_state | OTP | UVLO | latch_assert) & ~window_trip) begin
AIM.18.reason: When a hard fault and window_trip are both high in S_RUN, the FSM enters S_HICCUP instead of S_OFF. hiccup_active and state_out show the cool-down state for at least one clock, and a strike is counted for what should have been a shutdown.

AIM.19.description: In S_HICCUP the end of the cool-down outranks a hard fault, so a retry into S_SS wins over a shutdown
AIM.19.before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) begin
AIM.19.after: if ((~g_en | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) & ~hiccup_done) begin
AIM.19.reason: If a hard fault is present on the clock where hiccup_done rises, the FSM retries into S_SS instead of going to S_OFF, so ss_active and state_out show S_SS. If the fault was a one-clock latch_assert pulse, en rises again before latch_state is read back.

AIM.20.description: In S_SS ramp completion outranks the hard faults, so a fault at the end of the ramp still promotes the FSM to S_RUN
AIM.20.before: if (~g_en | OTP | latch_state | UVLO | latch_assert) begin
AIM.20.after: if ((~g_en | OTP | latch_state | UVLO | latch_assert) & ~SS_done) begin
AIM.20.reason: A hard fault on the clock where SS_done rises sends the FSM to S_RUN instead of S_OFF, so run_active pulses high. If the fault was a one-clock latch_assert, the FSM stays in S_RUN and en comes back at full duty.

AIM.21.description: The combinational en gating uses the physical switch alone, so a host disable over SPI waits for the FSM to reach S_OFF
AIM.21.reason: When spi_enable falls in S_SS or S_RUN with en_SW still high, en stays high for one more clock until state registers S_OFF, instead of dropping on the same clock.

AIM.22.description: hiccup_active is dropped as soon as the cool-down reports done, a clock before the FSM leaves S_HICCUP
AIM.22.reason: On the last clock of S_HICCUP, when hiccup_done is high, the hiccup_active port goes low while state_out still shows S_HICCUP. hiccup_timer then clears its counter and hiccup_done one clock earlier than it should.

AIM.23.description: Start-up from S_OFF checks only the physical switch and forgets the host enable over SPI
AIM.23.reason: With en_SW high and spi_enable low, the FSM leaves S_OFF for S_SS, and the S_SS hard-fault check sends it straight back. ss_active and state_out then toggle every clock while the host has the converter disabled.

AIM.24.description: In S_RUN either overcurrent window trip sends the FSM to S_HICCUP: the soft-start trip window_trip_SS is honoured outside S_SS
AIM.24.reason: In S_RUN with no hard faults, a window_trip_SS that stays high (for example a soft-start count held through the run) now moves the FSM to S_HICCUP. hiccup_active rises and en drops, when the FSM should stay in S_RUN.

AIM.25.description: Over-temperature in S_RUN is treated as a recoverable fault and sent through the S_HICCUP cool-down instead of straight to S_OFF
AIM.25.before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | UVLO | latch_assert) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (window_trip) begin
AIM.25.after: if (~g_en | latch_state | UVLO | latch_assert) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (OTP | window_trip) begin
AIM.25.reason: When OTP rises in S_RUN with enable high, state_out goes to S_HICCUP and hiccup_active pulses high for a clock before the S_HICCUP hard-fault check moves it to S_OFF. It should go to S_OFF directly.

AIM.26.description: At the end of the cool-down S_HICCUP retries straight into S_RUN when the soft-start handshake SS_done is still high, skipping the re-ramp
AIM.26.reason: When hiccup_done arrives with SS_done high and no hard faults, the FSM goes to S_RUN and run_active rises instead of ss_active. This breaks the rule that a retry always re-ramps.

AIM.27.description: The state register is clock-enabled by the converter enable, so it freezes instead of loading S_OFF when the enable is lost
AIM.27.reason: If en_SW or spi_enable drops in S_RUN, state_out and run_active stay at S_RUN instead of going to S_OFF. When the enable returns, the FSM resumes in S_RUN without a soft-start ramp.

AIM.28.description: The gate drive is re-enabled on the clock hiccup_done rises in S_HICCUP, a clock before the FSM has registered the retry into S_SS
AIM.28.reason: In S_HICCUP with enable high and no hard faults, en goes high as soon as hiccup_done rises while state_out still reads S_HICCUP. It should stay low until the FSM is in S_SS.

AIM.29.description: The gate drive is enabled in S_OFF as soon as the converter is enabled, a clock before the FSM has registered S_SS
AIM.29.reason: In S_OFF, when en_SW and spi_enable are high and no hard fault is present, en goes high on that clock while state_out still reads S_OFF and ss_active is low. The power stage then switches before soft start is active.

AIM.30.description: In S_SS either overcurrent window trip sends the FSM to S_HICCUP: the run-state trip window_trip is also honoured during soft start
AIM.30.reason: In S_SS with window_trip high and window_trip_SS low (no hard fault), the FSM goes to S_HICCUP instead of holding S_SS or going on to S_RUN. hiccup_active and state_out change, and en drops.

AIM.31.description: S_HICCUP retries only when the cool-down has elapsed and the run overcurrent trip has also cleared, as if a retry had to wait for the fault to go away
AIM.31.reason: In S_HICCUP with hiccup_done high and window_trip still high, the FSM stays in S_HICCUP instead of retrying into S_SS. hiccup_active stays high, ss_active and en stay low, and state_out holds S_HICCUP.

AIM.32.description: S_RUN is treated as valid only while the soft-start handshake SS_done is held, and drops back to S_SS when SS_done falls
AIM.32.after: end / else if (~SS_done) begin /  / next_state = S_SS; /  / end
AIM.32.reason: In S_RUN with no fault and no window trip, SS_done going low moves the FSM to S_SS instead of holding S_RUN. run_active falls, ss_active rises and state_out shows S_SS.

AIM.33.description: Reset puts the FSM in the S_HICCUP cool-down instead of S_OFF, as if power-up had to wait out a cool-down before the first start
AIM.33.reason: After reset, hiccup_active is high and state_out shows S_HICCUP instead of S_OFF. With the converter enabled, the first start waits for hiccup_done instead of going to S_SS on the next clock.

AIM.34.description: ss_active is decoded as 'power stage may switch', so it is also high in S_RUN
AIM.34.reason: In S_RUN, ss_active is high together with run_active, when it should be high only in S_SS.

AIM.35.description: UVLO during soft start is treated as a recoverable inrush brown-out and sent through the S_HICCUP cool-down instead of straight to S_OFF
AIM.35.before: if (~g_en | OTP | latch_state | UVLO | latch_assert) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (window_trip_SS) begin
AIM.35.after: if (~g_en | OTP | latch_state | latch_assert) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (window_trip_SS | UVLO) begin
AIM.35.reason: In S_SS, with UVLO high and the converter enabled and no other hard fault, the FSM goes to S_HICCUP instead of S_OFF. hiccup_active rises and state_out shows S_HICCUP for at least one clock.

AIM.36.description: latch_assert in S_RUN is treated as one more strike and sent to the S_HICCUP cool-down instead of forcing S_OFF
AIM.36.before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | UVLO | latch_assert) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (window_trip) begin
AIM.36.after: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | UVLO) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (window_trip | latch_assert) begin
AIM.36.reason: In S_RUN, with latch_assert high and no other hard fault, the FSM goes to S_HICCUP instead of S_OFF. hiccup_active rises and state_out shows S_HICCUP.

AIM.37.description: Start-up from S_OFF counts the overcurrent window trips as faults that must be absent, reading 'no fault present' as including them
AIM.37.reason: In S_OFF, with the converter enabled and no hard fault, but window_trip or window_trip_SS high, the FSM stays in S_OFF instead of going to S_SS. ss_active and en stay low.

AIM.38.description: Start-up from S_OFF waits for the soft-start handshake SS_done to be low, as if the ramp had to report its reset first
AIM.38.reason: In S_OFF, with the converter enabled and no fault but SS_done high, the FSM stays in S_OFF instead of going to S_SS. ss_active and en stay low until SS_done falls.

AIM.39.description: In S_HICCUP latch_assert only blocks the retry instead of forcing S_OFF, as if a strike-latched converter just stayed in the cool-down
AIM.39.before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (hiccup_done) begin
AIM.39.after: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | UVLO) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (hiccup_done & ~latch_assert) begin
AIM.39.reason: strike_counter raises latch_assert on entry to S_HICCUP when MAX_STRIKES is reached; the original FSM goes to S_OFF the next clock, while the mutant stays in S_HICCUP with hiccup_active high and state_out = S_HICCUP indefinitely (latch_assert is set-only).

AIM.40.description: Over-temperature during S_HICCUP is treated as part of the cool-down: the FSM stays in S_HICCUP until OTP clears instead of going to S_OFF
AIM.40.before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (hiccup_done) begin
AIM.40.after: if (~g_en | latch_state | latch_assert | UVLO) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (hiccup_done & ~OTP) begin
AIM.40.reason: With OTP asserted while in S_HICCUP, the original moves to S_OFF on the next clock; the mutant keeps hiccup_active high and state_out at S_HICCUP, then retries into S_SS once OTP falls and hiccup_done is high, without ever passing through S_OFF.

AIM.41.description: The host enable over SPI is treated as a start request checked only in S_OFF, so a host disable while ramping, running or in hiccup is ignored
AIM.41.reason: If spi_enable falls while the FSM is in S_SS or S_RUN with en_SW high, the original drops en at once and goes to S_OFF; the mutant keeps en high and stays in its state until the physical switch or a fault turns it off.
AIM.41.withdrawn: the per-state enable mutants combined: a host (AIM.41) or switch (AIM.76) disable ignored in S_SS, S_RUN and S_HICCUP gives the same wrong state as AIM.46/15/47 or AIM.55/50/56, so any test that kills one of those kills it

AIM.42.description: run_active is raised on the clock the ramp reports SS_done, a clock before the FSM has registered S_RUN
AIM.42.reason: In S_SS with SS_done high (and no fault), run_active goes high one clock before state_out shows S_RUN. It also pulses high when SS_done and window_trip_SS arrive together and the FSM goes to S_HICCUP instead.

AIM.43.description: ss_active is raised on the clock the cool-down reports hiccup_done, a clock before the FSM has registered the retry into S_SS
AIM.43.reason: In S_HICCUP with hiccup_done high, ss_active is high together with hiccup_active one clock before state_out shows S_SS. It also pulses when a hard fault arrives on that clock and sends the FSM to S_OFF instead.

AIM.44.description: hiccup_active is held until the cool-down timer drops hiccup_done, as if leaving S_HICCUP had to wait for the timer's acknowledge
AIM.44.reason: After the retry from S_HICCUP to S_SS, hiccup_active stays high while hiccup_done is still high, so it overlaps ss_active in S_SS. In the system this keeps hiccup_timer from ever clearing hiccup_done, so hiccup_active stays high through S_SS and S_RUN.

AIM.45.description: An overcurrent window trip during soft start only pauses the promotion to S_RUN and keeps the FSM ramping in S_SS, as if high current while the output capacitor charges were expected, instead of sending the converter into the S_HICCUP cool-down
AIM.45.reason: When window_trip_SS rises in S_SS, state_out stays at S_SS, ss_active and en stay high and hiccup_active never rises, so the gate drive keeps switching into the overcurrent. The FSM moves on to S_RUN once the soft-start window count falls below trip_ss while SS_done is high, so no cool-down or strike is ever taken.

AIM.46.description: In S_SS only the physical switch is checked for disable, so a host disable over SPI during soft start gates en but leaves the FSM ramping in S_SS
AIM.46.before: if (~g_en | OTP | latch_state | UVLO | latch_assert) begin
AIM.46.after: if (~en_SW | OTP | latch_state | UVLO | latch_assert) begin
AIM.46.reason: If spi_enable falls while the FSM is in S_SS (with en_SW still high), en drops through the combinational gating, but the FSM stays in S_SS. ss_active stays high and state_out reads S_SS, and on SS_done the FSM moves to S_RUN instead of S_OFF.

AIM.47.description: In S_HICCUP only the physical switch is checked for disable, so a host disable over SPI during the cool-down does not send the FSM to S_OFF and it still retries into S_SS
AIM.47.before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) begin
AIM.47.after: if (~en_SW | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) begin
AIM.47.reason: If spi_enable falls during S_HICCUP (with en_SW high), hiccup_active stays high instead of dropping. When hiccup_done arrives, the FSM retries into S_SS, so ss_active and state_out show soft start on a converter the host has disabled.

AIM.48.description: Input undervoltage in S_RUN is treated as a recoverable brown-out under load and sent through the S_HICCUP cool-down instead of straight to S_OFF
AIM.48.before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | UVLO | latch_assert) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (window_trip) begin
AIM.48.after: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (window_trip | UVLO) begin
AIM.48.reason: If UVLO asserts while regulating in S_RUN, the FSM goes to S_HICCUP instead of S_OFF: hiccup_active rises and state_out reads S_HICCUP. If UVLO has cleared by hiccup_done, the converter retries into S_SS on its own rather than restarting from S_OFF.

AIM.49.description: Start-up from S_OFF checks only the host enable over SPI and forgets the physical switch en_SW
AIM.49.reason: With spi_enable high, en_SW low and no fault, the FSM leaves S_OFF for S_SS. The next clock S_SS sees ~g_en and goes back to S_OFF, so ss_active and state_out toggle every clock while the switch is off, but en stays low.

AIM.50.description: In S_RUN only a host disable over SPI is checked: turning off the physical switch gates en but does not send the FSM to S_OFF
AIM.50.before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | UVLO | latch_assert) begin
AIM.50.after: if (~spi_enable | latch_state | OTP | UVLO | latch_assert) begin
AIM.50.reason: Turning en_SW off in S_RUN pulls en low but leaves state_out at S_RUN with run_active high. When the switch comes back on, en goes high again straight into S_RUN with no soft-start ramp.

AIM.51.description: The combinational en gating applies only the host enable, so turning off the physical switch waits for the FSM to register S_OFF
AIM.51.reason: When en_SW falls in S_SS or S_RUN, en stays high for one more clock until state becomes S_OFF, instead of dropping on the same clock.

AIM.52.description: Telemetry state_out reports S_OFF as soon as a hard fault gates en, instead of the registered present state
AIM.52.after: state_out     = (OTP | UVLO | latch_state | latch_assert) ? S_OFF : state;
AIM.52.reason: When OTP, UVLO, latch_state or latch_assert rises in S_SS, S_RUN or S_HICCUP, state_out reads S_OFF one clock before the state register does, while ss_active, run_active or hiccup_active still show the old state.

AIM.53.description: A start request blocked in S_OFF by OTP or UVLO is treated as a recoverable fault and sent into the S_HICCUP cool-down instead of holding S_OFF
AIM.53.after: else if (g_en & (OTP | UVLO)) begin /  / next_state = S_HICCUP; /  / end / else begin
AIM.53.reason: If the converter is enabled while OTP or UVLO is high, the FSM switches between S_OFF and S_HICCUP: hiccup_active and state_out pulse every other clock, and each entry counts as a strike, instead of the FSM staying in S_OFF.

AIM.54.description: Over-temperature during soft start is treated as a recoverable start-up stress and sent through the S_HICCUP cool-down instead of straight to S_OFF
AIM.54.before: if (~g_en | OTP | latch_state | UVLO | latch_assert) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (window_trip_SS) begin
AIM.54.after: if (~g_en | latch_state | UVLO | latch_assert) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (window_trip_SS | OTP) begin
AIM.54.reason: If OTP rises while the FSM is in S_SS, state_out goes to S_HICCUP and hiccup_active pulses (a strike gets counted) before the FSM reaches S_OFF. It should go straight to S_OFF with hiccup_active staying low.

AIM.55.description: In S_SS only a host disable over SPI is checked: turning off the physical switch during soft start gates en but leaves the FSM ramping in S_SS
AIM.55.before: if (~g_en | OTP | latch_state | UVLO | latch_assert) begin
AIM.55.after: if (~spi_enable | OTP | latch_state | UVLO | latch_assert) begin
AIM.55.reason: If en_SW falls while in S_SS with spi_enable high, en drops but state_out stays S_SS and ss_active stays high instead of going to S_OFF. The FSM then moves on to S_RUN when SS_done arrives.

AIM.56.description: In S_HICCUP only a host disable over SPI is checked: turning off the physical switch during the cool-down does not send the FSM to S_OFF
AIM.56.before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) begin
AIM.56.after: if (~spi_enable | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) begin
AIM.56.reason: If en_SW falls during S_HICCUP with spi_enable high, the FSM stays in S_HICCUP instead of going to S_OFF, and on hiccup_done it retries into S_SS (state_out S_SS, ss_active high) while the switch is still off.

AIM.57.description: Losing the enable during the cool-down only holds off the retry: the FSM waits in S_HICCUP until it is re-enabled instead of going to S_OFF
AIM.57.before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (hiccup_done) begin
AIM.57.after: if (latch_state | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (hiccup_done & g_en) begin
AIM.57.reason: If en_SW or spi_enable falls in S_HICCUP, state_out stays S_HICCUP and hiccup_active stays high instead of going to S_OFF. When the converter is re-enabled after hiccup_done, it retries straight into S_SS from S_HICCUP.

AIM.58.description: Input undervoltage during the cool-down is treated as extending the cool-down: the FSM stays in S_HICCUP until UVLO clears instead of going to S_OFF
AIM.58.before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (hiccup_done) begin
AIM.58.after: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (hiccup_done & ~UVLO) begin
AIM.58.reason: If UVLO rises in S_HICCUP, state_out stays S_HICCUP and hiccup_active stays high instead of going to S_OFF. Once UVLO clears after hiccup_done, the FSM retries into S_SS directly from S_HICCUP.

AIM.59.description: ss_active is decoded as 'a soft-start sequence is under way', so it is also high during the S_HICCUP cool-down that leads into the re-ramp
AIM.59.reason: In S_HICCUP the ss_active port is high instead of low. That makes soft_start ramp and fault_arbiter count soft-start faults during the cool-down, so window_trip_SS can fire there and the retry into S_SS starts with a ramp that has already advanced.

AIM.60.description: run_active treats the hiccup cool-down as a pause inside regulation, so it is also high in S_HICCUP
AIM.60.reason: After a window_trip from S_RUN, run_active stays high through the whole S_HICCUP cool-down. soft_start then keeps SS_done and the full ceiling, so the retry is promoted out of S_SS without a fresh ramp. The strike_counter clean-run streak also keeps counting while the gate drive is off.

AIM.61.description: hiccup_active is decoded as 'a hiccup retry is in progress', so it also covers the re-ramp in S_SS, including the first start from S_OFF
AIM.61.reason: Whenever the FSM is in S_SS, hiccup_active is high. hiccup_timer then times a cool-down during soft start and does not clear hiccup_done when S_HICCUP is left for S_SS. strike_counter also sees an S_HICCUP entry on an ordinary start from S_OFF.

AIM.62.description: Losing the enable in S_RUN is handled like an overcurrent trip and sent through S_HICCUP, as if a disable under load had to cool down before turning off
AIM.62.before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | UVLO | latch_assert) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (window_trip) begin
AIM.62.after: if (latch_state | OTP | UVLO | latch_assert) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (window_trip | ~g_en) begin
AIM.62.reason: Turning the converter off (en_SW or spi_enable low) while in S_RUN now registers S_HICCUP for one clock before S_OFF: hiccup_active pulses high and state_out shows S_HICCUP, which the strike counter and hiccup timer see as a hiccup entry.

AIM.63.description: During soft start the latch read-back latch_state is treated as an overvoltage overshoot of the ramp, a recoverable event sent to the S_HICCUP cool-down, instead of a hard fault forcing S_OFF
AIM.63.before: if (~g_en | OTP | latch_state | UVLO | latch_assert) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (window_trip_SS) begin
AIM.63.after: if (~g_en | OTP | UVLO | latch_assert) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (window_trip_SS | latch_state) begin
AIM.63.reason: If latch_state rises while the FSM is in S_SS, the FSM goes to S_HICCUP for one clock (hiccup_active high, state_out = S_HICCUP, counted as a strike) before S_HICCUP's hard-fault test sends it to S_OFF, instead of going directly to S_OFF.

AIM.64.description: The gate drive in S_SS is decoded as 'ramp still in progress', so it drops on the clock the ramp reports SS_done, before the FSM has registered S_RUN
AIM.64.reason: At the end of every soft start, on the one clock where state is still S_SS and soft_start has already raised SS_done, en goes low for one clock before S_RUN turns it back on. The output therefore has a one-clock gate-drive dropout on every hand-over from soft start to regulation.

AIM.65.description: Telemetry state_out reports the hiccup cool-down as S_OFF, because the power stage is off in both, instead of the registered present state
AIM.65.reason: Whenever the FSM is in S_HICCUP after an overcurrent window trip, state_out reads S_OFF (2'b00) instead of S_HICCUP (2'b11) for the whole cool-down, while hiccup_active is high.

AIM.66.description: In S_RUN the latch read-back latch_state is treated as a recoverable overshoot from a load step and sent to the S_HICCUP cool-down instead of forcing S_OFF
AIM.66.before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | UVLO | latch_assert) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (window_trip) begin
AIM.66.after: if (~g_en | OTP | UVLO | latch_assert) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (window_trip | latch_state) begin
AIM.66.reason: When latch_state rises in S_RUN, the FSM registers S_HICCUP: hiccup_active goes high and state_out shows S_HICCUP for a clock before S_HICCUP's own check sends it to S_OFF, instead of going straight to S_OFF.

AIM.67.description: In S_HICCUP the latch read-back latch_state only holds off the retry, as if the latch were left over from the fault being cooled down, instead of forcing S_OFF
AIM.67.before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (hiccup_done) begin
AIM.67.after: if (~g_en | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (hiccup_done & ~latch_state) begin
AIM.67.reason: If latch_state goes high during the cool-down, the FSM stays in S_HICCUP (hiccup_active high, state_out S_HICCUP) instead of going to S_OFF. When the latch clears after hiccup_done, it retries into S_SS on its own.

AIM.68.description: ss_active is raised in S_OFF as soon as the converter is enabled, as a start request to soft start, a clock before the FSM has registered S_SS
AIM.68.reason: In S_OFF with en_SW and spi_enable high, ss_active rises a clock before state_out shows S_SS. If a hard fault (OTP, UVLO, latch) blocks start-up, ss_active stays high in S_OFF for as long as the enable is held.

AIM.69.description: In S_RUN the gate drive is made to depend on the soft-start handshake SS_done, as if regulation were allowed to switch only while the ramp still reports done
AIM.69.reason: In S_RUN with no fault, en follows SS_done: if SS_done falls or is only a pulse, en drops while the FSM stays in S_RUN and run_active stays high.

AIM.70.description: Losing the enable during soft start is handled like a soft-start overcurrent trip and sent through S_HICCUP, as if an aborted ramp had to cool down before turning off
AIM.70.before: if (~g_en | OTP | latch_state | UVLO | latch_assert) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (window_trip_SS) begin
AIM.70.after: if (OTP | latch_state | UVLO | latch_assert) begin /  / next_state = S_OFF; /  / end / else if (window_trip_SS | ~g_en) begin
AIM.70.reason: When en_SW or spi_enable drops in S_SS, the FSM registers S_HICCUP: hiccup_active pulses high and state_out shows S_HICCUP for a clock before S_HICCUP's own check sends it to S_OFF, instead of going straight to S_OFF.

AIM.71.description: Start-up from S_OFF tests the gated gate-drive enable en instead of the combined converter enable g_en, confusing the output enable with the enable request
AIM.71.reason: In S_OFF en_from_state is 0 so en is always low, and the FSM never leaves S_OFF: with en_SW and spi_enable high and no fault, ss_active, en and state_out stay at S_OFF instead of starting soft start.

AIM.72.description: The disable test in S_HICCUP uses the gated gate-drive enable en instead of the converter enable g_en, so the cool-down's own gate-drive-off reads as a disable
AIM.72.before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) begin
AIM.72.after: if (~en | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) begin
AIM.72.reason: en is always low in S_HICCUP, so after a window trip the FSM leaves for S_OFF one clock after entering S_HICCUP, then restarts into S_SS without waiting for hiccup_done: hiccup_active lasts one clock and the cool-down is skipped.

AIM.73.description: ss_active is decoded as 'ramping with the gate drive on', so the combinational fault gating of en also drops it before the FSM leaves S_SS
AIM.73.reason: When a hard fault or disable arrives during soft start, ss_active falls on the same clock as en instead of a clock later when the FSM registers S_OFF. The ramp and the soft-start overcurrent window are therefore cleared one clock early.

AIM.74.description: hiccup_active is decoded as 'cool-down still running', so a hard fault or disable drops it combinationally before the FSM leaves S_HICCUP
AIM.74.reason: When OTP, UVLO, the latch or a disable arrives during the cool-down, hiccup_active falls on that clock instead of a clock later with the registered move to S_OFF. The hiccup timer and strike counter are therefore released early.

AIM.75.description: Every start from S_OFF goes through the S_HICCUP cool-down before soft start, as if each restart after a shutdown needed the same off-time as a fault retry
AIM.75.reason: When the converter is enabled with no fault present, en stays low and hiccup_active goes high for a whole cool-down interval before S_SS and the gate drive begin. On every start the strike counter also sees S_HICCUP entered.

AIM.76.description: The physical switch en_SW is treated as a start request checked only in S_OFF, so turning it off while ramping, running or in hiccup is ignored
AIM.76.reason: In S_SS, S_RUN or S_HICCUP, turning en_SW low no longer pulls en low or sends the FSM to S_OFF. The converter keeps switching, and a hiccup retries into S_SS, until the host disables it over SPI or a hard fault occurs.
AIM.76.withdrawn: the per-state enable mutants combined: a host (AIM.41) or switch (AIM.76) disable ignored in S_SS, S_RUN and S_HICCUP gives the same wrong state as AIM.46/15/47 or AIM.55/50/56, so any test that kills one of those kills it

AIM.77.description: Telemetry state_out reports S_RUN as soon as the ramp reports SS_done, instead of the registered present state
AIM.77.reason: On the clock SS_done rises in S_SS, state_out reads S_RUN a clock before the FSM registers S_RUN. If window_trip_SS fires on that same clock, state_out shows S_RUN while the FSM goes from S_SS to S_HICCUP.

AIM.78.description: The combined converter enable g_en is registered instead of combinational, so the switch and host enables reach the gate drive and the FSM a clock late
AIM.78.before: always_comb begin /  / /* / Purpose: / --- / Combine the two enables. The physical switch and the host must both allow the / converter to run; either one alone turns it off. / */ /  / g_en = spi_enable & en_SW;
AIM.78.after: always_ff @(posedge clk) begin /  / /* / Purpose: / --- / Combine the two enables. The physical switch and the host must both allow the / converter to run; either one alone turns it off. / */ /  / g_en <= spi_enable & en_SW;
AIM.78.reason: If en_SW or spi_enable falls in S_SS or S_RUN, en stays high for one more clock and the FSM registers S_OFF a clock late. A start from S_OFF also moves to S_SS a clock after the enable rises.

AIM.79.description: The LM5106 enable en is registered to give a glitch-free gate drive, so it follows the state and the fault inputs one clock late
AIM.79.before: always_comb begin /  / /* / Purpose: / --- / Drive the LM5106 enable. Gated by the fault inputs directly as well as by the / state, so a trip pulls the gate drive low combinationally, on the same clock, / instead of a clock later when the FSM has registered S_OFF. / */ /  / en = g_en & en_from_state & ~OTP & ~latch_state & ~UVLO & ~latch_assert;
AIM.79.after: always_ff @(posedge clk) begin /  / /* / Purpose: / --- / Drive the LM5106 enable. Gated by the fault inputs directly as well as by the / state, so a trip pulls the gate drive low combinationally, on the same clock, / instead of a clock later when the FSM has registered S_OFF. / */ /  / en <= g_en & en_from_state & ~OTP & ~latch_state & ~UVLO & ~latch_assert;
AIM.79.reason: en rises one clock after the FSM registers S_SS. It stays high for one clock after S_RUN gives way to S_HICCUP on window_trip. After OTP, UVLO, latch_state, latch_assert or a disable, it drops a clock late instead of on the same clock.
